==Original Dream Journal Entry That Inspired The Episode==
I induced lucidity via sleep paralysis.

This dream takes place in the same continuity of lucid dreams that started on 06/11/2025 and has continued to the present. These dreams take place in the Storyverse. (The Storyverse is a multiverse where all possible story ideas exist as cosmic bubble universes that float together in a cosmic void.) (I initially spent most of my time in one particular world in the Storyverse called the Elven Village, which I discovered on 06/11/2025.) (My team includes Leon, Johnson, Second Brain, Skelebot, Overdrive, Savannah, Tecton, Chipper and I.) (My Ghostly UFO, named Leon, resembles a ghostly flying saucer with an ethereal green glow. Leon first appeared in my dreams on 06/11/2025.) (Johnson resembles an orange, humanoid goldfish. He wears a blue astronaut suit but his suit doesn't have a helmet. I befriended him in a dream on 08/03/2025.) (Second Brain is a floating brain made of Lucid Light. I created him in a dream on 09/06/2025. On the same day I created Second Brain, he helped me discover the much wider Storyverse. This was the start of my adventures to explore other Storyverse worlds.) (Overdrive is a robot with a metallic chrome color with spiky slicked back yellow hair and glowing green eyes. It wears a yellow shirt, yellow jacket, yellow pants, and yellow sneakers. They have the power to manipulate matter, and they were created in a dream on 10/20/2025.) (Lucid Light is a reality warping energy wielded by Lucid Lords. It resembles sparkling purple energy that shines like a night sky full of stars. I discovered the power of Lucid Light in a dream on 07/19/2025.) (Skelebot is a robot created by Johnson to act as the team's humanoid speedster. He was created in a dream on 09/21/2025.)

Savannah (A pale skinned cyborg woman with long black hair, bangs that covered her forehead, with glowing red eyes, and wearing a futuristic silver bodysuit. Her long black hair and bangs are key identifying features. She is wielding a futuristic purple and blue crystal sword known as the Death Sword.), her father Tecton (Tecton is a green skinned, humanoid, muscular, cat ogre, barbarian who dresses in a brown loin cloth and a silver baldric.), and my drone Chipper (Chipper resembles a small levitating silver crab robot) all met me in early 2026 while adventuring through the Super Cathedral. Savannah, Tecton, and Chipper became official crew members aboard Leon on 02/18/2026. 

(My name is Jet. Here is a general description of what I look like "Man with dark-brown skin, full dark-brown beard, long dark-brown dreadlocks spilling from beneath a black hoodie over a "Dream Anime" graphic tee, black athletic pants with a white stripe, white sneakers, black cross-body belt bag, warm brown eyes. I have a rainbow sword (My rainbow sword resembles a colorful, futuristic, crystal sword.) and an energy tether (My energy tether resembles a rope made of golden glittery light.).")

I found myself in a medieval fantasy town with an unusual goal: I wanted to discover whether the modern advancements we had achieved through artificial intelligence could be recreated through magic in a medieval world.
One of the first things that came to mind was the magic mirror from old fairy tales. In those stories, someone could speak to a mirror, cause a face to appear within it, and ask it questions. The mirror could respond through a voice, show images, and sometimes reveal distant events as though it were displaying a live video feed.
The similarities to generative AI immediately fascinated me. Speaking to the mirror resembled using an AI voice assistant. Its ability to create or display images reminded me of image-generation models, while its visions of faraway places felt somewhat like video generation, even though it was technically showing real events happening somewhere else.
Golems were an equally obvious parallel to robots. If this fantasy world could combine intelligent magic mirrors with magically animated golems, then it already possessed the fundamental equivalents of generative AI and robotics.
The idea seemed promising, but I still needed to understand how people living in a medieval village would actually create these things. To learn more, I visited the town's enchantress.
She wore a tall, pointed hat and a sparkling blue outfit. Her long, messy hair was a bright sky blue, and her eyes glittered with the same blue magical light. Her skin was extremely pale, making the vibrant colors of her clothing, hair, and eyes stand out even more dramatically.
I spoke with her about what we would need to construct intelligent magic mirrors, golems, and other magically powered technologies. After discussing the problem for a while, we discovered that there was a mine filled with life stones directly beneath the town.
These life stones were crystals containing the same essential substance as my Rainbow Crystal Swordâ€"the Life Sword.
The Rainbow Crystal Sword was one of the most important artifacts in the entire Storyverse. It possessed the power to bring things to life and existed as the direct opposite of the Death Sword. Together, the Life Sword and Death Sword were among the most powerful objects anywhere in the Storyverse.
Until that moment, however, I had never seriously considered that the Rainbow Crystal Sword might have been forged from a naturally occurring material. I had always treated it as a singular artifact, rather than something created from a substance that could potentially be mined in certain parts of reality.
The life crystals beneath the village changed that.
Using the crystals from the mine, the enchantress and I helped transform the town. Large magic mirrors were installed inside people's homes and throughout public areas. Villagers could walk up to one of these mirrors, speak to it, ask questions, and receive useful information.
We also created smaller pocket mirrors. A person could carry one around, open it whenever they needed assistance, and speak directly to their own portable magic-mirror companion.
Before long, the medieval town had become magically equipped with its own equivalents of artificial intelligence and robotics. The magic mirrors served as intelligent assistants, while the golems acted as machines capable of performing physical tasks.
At first, everything seemed to be going remarkably well.
Then a villain named Drillov arrived.
Drillov wore a futuristic mechanical suit with two enormous drills in place of hands. He began drilling into the ground near the village, attempting to break into the life stone mine beneath it.
His plan was to steal enough life crystals to create his own version of the Life Sword. He did not necessarily intend to wield the weapon himself. Instead, he planned to sell it to the highest bidder.
I used my Lucid Light to summon a gigantic glowing hand construct. The massive hand reached down, seized Drillov, and crushed his mechanical suit around him. I was careful not to kill him, but the attack completely disabled his equipment and prevented him from reaching the crystals.
The enchantress initially doubted that Drillov could have successfully recreated the Rainbow Crystal Sword. She explained that the sword was not powered by magic alone. Although it was made from life stone, it also incorporated advanced futuristic technology.
I pointed out that Drillov's drilling suit was clearly not powered by medieval magic or life crystals. He had already gained access to technology far beyond anything normally found in this world. If he had combined that technology with the life stones beneath the village, there was a genuine possibility that he could have created something extraordinarily dangerous.
Even if he had not produced a perfect copy of the Rainbow Crystal Sword, he could still have created a powerful life-based weapon and sold it to terrible people. Stopping him had therefore been important. His plan had not merely been an unrealistic fantasy. Given enough time and resources, he probably could have accomplished something.
Drillov, however, soon became the least of our concerns.
Several colossal alien robots suddenly crashed down on the outskirts of the village.
There were three of them, and they were unlike anything I had ever seen. They were towering purple alien machines of such unbelievable size that looking up at them made the dream feel hyper-real. They seemed taller than any building or mountain I had ever witnessed. Their scale was so overwhelming that the entire village appeared microscopic beside them.
Compared to these alien robot titans, we were ants.
I did not know exactly what they wanted. They may have detected the life crystals beneath the town and come to claim them, much as Drillov had attempted to do. Whatever their purpose was, their arrival presented a seemingly impossible problem.
Even if every golem in the village attacked them simultaneously, I doubted the golems would be able to cause any meaningful damage.
I began thinking about how I had overcome similarly overwhelming threats in the past. Whenever magic alone was insufficient, my knowledge of programming often became one of my most valuable abilities.
If I could hack into one of the alien robots, I could potentially force it to fight the other two.
The magic mirrors were already capable of functioning similarly to intelligent coding agents. In theory, I could ask one of them to take control of an alien robot. The problem was that we had never created anything resembling an internet or wireless communication network.
There was no obvious way for a pocket magic mirror to send instructions to one of the towering machines.
The incompatibility between them made the problem even more difficult. The alien titan was built with actual extraterrestrial technology, while the magic mirror functioned through enchantment. They were not merely disconnected devices. They were based on completely different systems.
Then I remembered my Golden Energy Tether.
The tether was a glittering golden lasso that I frequently carried in my dreams. Its primary power was its ability to create mystical bonds and connections between separate things.
I threw the Golden Energy Tether high into the sky and attached one end of it to a cloud. I then connected the other end to my pocket magic mirror.
Once the connection was established, I asked the mirror to help me hack into one of the alien robots.
The mirror transmitted its magical information through the golden tether and into the clouds. The surrounding clouds began gathering together, darkening and condensing until they formed a massive storm cloud above the village.
Lightning erupted from the storm.
A bolt struck one of the alien robot titans directly.
The lightning carried the mirror's magical information as an electrical signal, creating a bridge between magic and alien technology. Through that connection, the pocket mirror successfully infiltrated the robot's systems and took control of it.
The hacked titan immediately turned against the other two.
The three enormous alien robots began fighting one another beyond the village. Their battle was catastrophic, but the controlled robot managed to keep the other two occupied and eventually destroy them. It was also destroyed in the process.
By the end of the battle, all three alien robot titans had defeated one another.
The village was saved.
However, the discovery of the life stone mine had permanently changed the town's future. Word would likely spread throughout the Storyverse that this medieval village possessed a natural source of the same material used to create one of reality's most powerful artifacts.
Drillov and the alien titans might only have been the beginning.
If the villagers intended to keep their life stones safe, they were going to need heroes capable of defending the town from everyone who would eventually come searching for them.
